school.tagged_body:
The Kimchi Notebook

Every year on the last Saturday of November, Yerin's {{v:whole}} family met at her grandmother's house for {{v:gimjang}}. Gimjang is the day {{g:of making kimchi|전치사 of + 동명사: ~하는 (날)}} for winter.

This year, {{g:there were 50 heads of cabbage|there were + 복수 명사: ~이 있었다 (head of cabbage: 배추 한 포기)}} in the {{v:yard}}. Yerin {{v:sighed}}. "Grandma, {{g:why don't we just buy|Why don't we + 동사원형?: 우리 ~하는 게 어때? (제안)}} kimchi at the store? It's {{g:so much easier|much + 비교급: 훨씬 더 ~한 (비교급 강조)}}."

Her grandmother smiled, but she didn't answer. She just {{g:gave Yerin a pair of rubber gloves|4형식: give + 간접목적어(사람) + 직접목적어(사물)}}.

All morning, they {{v:salted}} {{v:cabbage}}. They also {{v:mixed}} red pepper {{v:powder}} with {{v:garlic}}, {{v:ginger}}, and fish {{v:sauce}}. By lunchtime, Yerin's {{v:back}} hurt. She {{g:stopped complaining|stop + -ing: ~하던 것을 멈추다}}, but only because she was {{g:too tired to talk|too + 형용사 + to부정사: 너무 ~해서 …할 수 없다}}.

Then her grandmother {{g:began to put|begin + to부정사: ~하기 시작하다}} the kimchi into boxes. Three boxes were for three {{v:neighbors}}. They lived {{v:alone}}. Five boxes were for the children's {{v:center}} down the street.

"I make kimchi like this every year. I started 50 years ago," her grandmother said. "My mother {{g:used to do|used to + 동사원형: (과거에) ~하곤 했다}} the same. {{t:Gimjang is not just about kimchi. It's about sharing}}."

That night, Yerin opened a new {{v:notebook}}. She {{v:wrote down}} every {{v:step}} of her grandmother's {{v:recipe}}. On the first page, she wrote, "{{t:Grandma's Kimchi – for sharing}}."

choices: a sign that Yerin plans to publish the recipe for profit
proof that Yerin still disagrees with her grandmother
a reminder to buy kimchi next winter
evidence that Yerin has embraced and will continue the family's tradition
a list of people who received the kimchi
questions.answer: evidence that Yerin has embraced and will continue the family's tradition
questions.explanation: 첫 장에 "for sharing" → 나눔의 전통을 받아들이고 이어 가겠다는 표시.

questions.q: Which sentence uses 'lie' correctly, as in '50 heads of cabbage lay stacked in the yard'?
choices: The book laid open on the desk all night.
The book lain open on the desk all night.
The book lay open on the desk all night.
The book lied open on the desk all night.
The book lying open on the desk all night.
questions.answer: The book lay open on the desk all night.
questions.explanation: lie(놓여 있다)-lay-lain. 과거형은 lay. (laid는 lay(놓다)의 과거형)

questions.q: 'No fewer than 50 heads of cabbage' is closest in meaning to ____.
choices: fewer than 50 heads of cabbage
at most 50 heads of cabbage
not even 50 heads of cabbage
only a few heads of cabbage
as many as 50 heads of cabbage
questions.answer: as many as 50 heads of cabbage
questions.explanation: no fewer than = 무려 ~이나(as many as) → 많다는 것을 강조한다.

questions.q: Which 'while' expresses contrast, as in 'while five boxes were set aside for the children's center'?
choices: My brother loves meat, while I prefer vegetables.
I fell asleep while watching TV.
While I was cooking, the phone rang.
Please wait here for a while.
She read a book while waiting for the bus.
questions.answer: My brother loves meat, while I prefer vegetables.
questions.explanation: 대조의 while: ~인 반면. 나머지는 시간(~하는 동안) 또는 명사(a while).

questions.q: Which statement is NOT true according to the story?
choices: Yerin's grandmother has prepared kimchi in this manner for half a century.
They combined red pepper powder with garlic, ginger, and fish sauce.
Yerin's grandmother learned gimjang from a cooking class.
One box was designated for each of three neighbors who lived by themselves.
Yerin documented every step of her grandmother's recipe.
questions.answer: Yerin's grandmother learned gimjang from a cooking class.
questions.explanation: 할머니의 어머니도 똑같이 했다고 했다. 요리 수업 이야기는 없다.

essays.q: Summarize the story in three English sentences: (1) Yerin's initial attitude, (2) the turning point, and (3) the meaning of the ending.
essays.sampleAnswer: At first, Yerin heaved a sigh and suggested purchasing kimchi because it would be considerably more convenient. After a long morning of work, she watched her grandmother pack kimchi for neighbors who lived alone and for a children's center, and learned that gimjang has always been about sharing. By inscribing "for sharing" in her new recipe notebook, Yerin showed that she had embraced the tradition and intended to carry it on.
essays.rubric: ① 처음 태도 ② 전환점(나눔을 봄) ③ 결말의 의미 ④ 영어 3문장, 정확성

essays.q: 우리말로 쓰시오: 이 글에서 할머니가 김장의 의미를 "말로 설명하지 않고 보여 준" 방식을 설명하고, 이 방식이 예린이의 변화에 어떤 영향을 주었는지 지문에 근거해 쓰시오.
essays.sampleAnswer: 할머니는 예린이의 질문에 대답하지 않고 고무장갑을 건넨 뒤, 함께 김장을 하고 김치를 이웃과 아동센터에 나누는 모습을 직접 보여 주었다. 설명이 아니라 경험으로 의미를 알게 했기 때문에, 예린이는 스스로 나눔의 가치를 깨닫고 그날 밤 레시피를 꼼꼼히 기록하며 첫 장에 "for sharing"이라고 적었다.
essays.rubric: ① 보여 주는 방식(침묵·장갑·나눔) ② 예린이의 변화(기록·for sharing) ③ 지문 근거

essays.q: 다음 문장을 so ~ that 구문으로 바꿔 쓰시오. 'She was too exhausted to utter a word.'
essays.sampleAnswer: She was so exhausted that she couldn't utter a word.
essays.rubric: ① so exhausted ② that she ③ couldn't (could not) utter a word

essays.q: 다음 우리말을 영어로 쓰시오. '김장은 결코 단지 김치에 관한 것이었던 적이 없다.' <조건> 현재완료, never, merely를 사용할 것
essays.sampleAnswer: Gimjang has never been merely about kimchi.
essays.rubric: ① has never been ② merely ③ about kimchi

essays.q: Should traditions like gimjang be kept even if buying the food is more convenient? Give your opinion with a reason in 3–4 English sentences.
essays.sampleAnswer: I think traditions like gimjang should be kept. Buying kimchi is convenient, but it cannot give us the experience of working and sharing together. As the story shows, gimjang connects family members and neighbors. These values are more important than saving time.
essays.rubric: ① 입장 ② 이유(지문 활용 가능) ③ 영어 3~4문장, 정확성
